crops.name: Maize
crops.summary: High-yielding cereal staple critical for food security and farm income in Oyo State; sensitive to prolonged dry spells during tasseling and silking.

oyoPlantingWindows.earlySeason: March – April (after steady onset of rains)

crops.rootCharacteristics: Fibrous shallow-to-medium root system concentrated in top 30–60 cm; high nutrient uptake demand, especially nitrogen.

nitrogenFixingPotential.managementCaveat: Requires external nitrogen replenishment via legume rotation residue, compost, or targeted mineral fertilizer.

soilHealthContributions: Produces substantial stover biomass that can reduce surface runoff if retained as mulch rather than burned.
Deepening root channels moderately improve topsoil aeration when intercropped or rotated.
managementRequirements: Timely weeding within the first 3–6 weeks after emergence to avoid severe yield loss.
Split nitrogen application or preceding legume residue retention depending on soil test status.
Ensure well-drained seedbeds to prevent waterlogging during peak Oyo rainy months.
pestAndDiseaseRisks: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) whorl feeding during vegetative stages.
Striga hermonthica parasitic weed pressure under continuous cereal monocropping.
Maize Streak Virus (MSV) transmitted by Cicadulina leafhoppers.
growingTips: Plant at onset of steady rains (avoid dry-planting before reliable moisture).
Use improved drought-tolerant and Striga-resistant Oyo-adapted varieties (e.g., SAMMAZ / IITA lines).
Avoid continuous maize-after-maize where soil N and Striga pressure are unmanaged.

crops.name: Cowpea
crops.summary: Drought-tolerant grain legume valued for protein nutrition, rapid ground cover, and potential biological nitrogen fixation when properly managed.

oyoPlantingWindows.lateSeason: August – mid-September (preferred in Oyo to harvest in dry weather)

crops.rootCharacteristics: Deep taproot capable of reaching 100+ cm; supports drought resilience and forms root nodules with Bradyrhizobium bacteria.

nitrogenFixingPotential.managementCaveat: Introducing a legume does not automatically guarantee improved soil fertility or higher yields. Net N benefit depends on retaining crop haulms/biomass, adequate soil phosphorus, effective nodulation, and local soil pH.

soilHealthContributions: Rapid canopy closure suppresses weeds and reduces raindrop impact erosion.
Breaks cereal pest and Striga life cycles when rotated after maize.
managementRequirements: Avoid waterlogged soils; cowpea is susceptible to root rot in standing water.
Monitor flowering and podding closely for insect pests.
Retain haulms or incorporate residues post-harvest to preserve organic matter.
pestAndDiseaseRisks: Maruca vitrata (pod borer) and flower thrips during reproductive stages.
Cowpea bruchid (Callosobruchus maculatus) during post-harvest storage.
growingTips: Late-season planting in Oyo helps pods mature as rains taper off, reducing fungal rot.
Moderate phosphorus availability supports stronger root nodulation.
Rotate with maize to disrupt Fall Armyworm and Striga buildup.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.summary: High-value commercial and soil-building legume suitable for Oyo State derived-savanna zones, requiring adequate moisture during pod fill.

oyoPlantingWindows.lateSeason: Mid-July – early August (depending on variety maturity)

crops.rootCharacteristics: Moderately deep taproot with lateral roots in top 45 cm; forms nitrogen-fixing nodules with compatible Bradyrhizobium japonicum strains.

nitrogenFixingPotential.estimateKgHa: 30–80 kg N/ha fixed (subject to harvest removal)
nitrogenFixingPotential.managementCaveat: Grain harvest removes substantial nitrogen; soil fertility gains occur mainly when residues remain on-field and promiscuous varieties or rhizobium inoculants are paired with sufficient phosphorus and near-neutral soil pH.

soilHealthContributions: Dense leaf litter drop at maturity enriches topsoil organic matter.
Disrupts maize pest cycles and suppresses Striga germination via trap-cropping effect.
managementRequirements: Use promiscuous-nodulating Nigerian varieties (e.g., TGx lines) or apply approved inoculant.
Soil pH below 5.5 can limit nodulation; verify pH via laboratory testing before scaling.
Harvest promptly at physiological maturity to avoid pod shattering.
pestAndDiseaseRisks: Asian soybean rust (Phakopsora pachyrhizi) during humid periods.
Rapid seed viability loss if stored in humid conditions.
growingTips: Plant when topsoil moisture is reliable to ensure uniform germination.
Avoid acidic soils without liming or organic amendment.
Strong commercial off-take market in Oyo agro-processing corridors.

provenance.datasetName: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources)
provenance.role: Historical daily meteorology, solar irradiance & MERRA-2 soil wetness
provenance.limitations: Grid-cell average (~55 km) does not capture plot-level microclimate or localized convective thunderstorms. Soil wetness is model-assimilated (MERRA-2), not an in-situ probe.

provenance.datasetName: NASA GPM IMERG (Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM)
provenance.role: Regional precipitation pattern validation & convective storm context
provenance.limitations: Satellite infrared/microwave estimates can under- or over-estimate brief tropical convective showers; ground rain-gauge confirmation is advised.

provenance.role: Topsoil moisture context (0–5 cm sensing depth)
provenance.limitations: Measures only the top 5 cm of soil; dense maize canopy and regional averaging reduce plot-specific accuracy.

strategies.label: Existing Practice (Continuous Maize)
benefits: Familiar single-crop workflow and consistent maize grain output when inputs are high.
risks: Accelerates nitrogen depletion and elevates Striga hermonthica and Fall Armyworm carryover.
Lower canopy ground cover increases topsoil erosion risk during heavy Oyo storms.
evidence: NASA POWER observed 26.2°C mean temp and 88% surface soil wetness across 7 days.
Continuous cereal monocropping lacks biological nitrogen replacement (0 kg N/ha fixed).

strategies.label: Balanced Legume Rotation
benefits: Cowpea provides rapid ground cover (erosion control) and drought resilience in dry spells.
Breaks cereal pest and Striga weed cycles between maize seasons.
Retains maize as the core household food-security and staple grain crop.
risks: Legume nitrogen benefit is NOT automatic: removing all haulms or lacking phosphorus/nodulation reduces net soil gain.
Cowpea flowering requires timely pest scouting for Maruca pod borer and thrips.

recommendedActions: Review Strategy D (Maize → Cowpea → Soybean) with your local Oyo State ADP extension officer before seed procurement.
Schedule a laboratory soil NPK & organic matter test to raise analysis confidence above 85%.
Monitor whorl-stage maize weekly for Fall Armyworm and scout cowpea/soybean at flowering.
Retain legume haulms/stover on-field after harvest rather than burning to support organic matter.
